title: AMD has patched its SSD-eating GPU driver bug with an optional Adrenalin update for RX 7000-series graphics cards and above
summary: It looks like it's got some quirks of its own, though.
body: I reported earlier this week on a bug within AMD's GPU driver suite , wherein a misfiring utility was accused of making huge amounts of erroneous storage writes. Some AMD graphics card owners reported their SSD health dropping by up to 1% per month, but a fix has finally arrived. AMD Adrenalin Edition 26.11.1 is an optional update, which means you'll need to download the installer yourself. However, according to the topline notes, the update fixes "excessive writes to the system drive" at idle for Radeon RX 7000-series graphics cards and above. AMD's wording suggests that older GPUs might not be affected by the bug, but some of the user reports mention RX 6000-series cards, so it's unclear if a fix for earlier models is still in the works. I also think it's a slightly odd move to make this an "optional" update, given the severity of some of the reports, though this is often how AMD deals with getting fixes out in between official driver releases—by the looks of the known issues, this interim driver might still need some work before it's patched into the next full release. AMD lists a litany of potential issues with various games, including crashes and driver timeouts in Assassin's…

title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly had an 'intimate relationship' with a second Nvidia employee, according to reports
summary: The report is based on information from "two people familiar with the matter."
body: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly had an "intimate relationship" with a second Nvidia employee, according to Reuters . This new allegation comes after Huang's resignation yesterday, following his admission of an affair , believed to be with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, and a New York Times report of another extramarital affair with Nvidia VP Kimberly Powell. Reuters has chosen not to name the second Nvidia employee in question, but says the information comes from "two people familiar with the matter." Huang's resignation from Nvidia came as a shock to many yesterday , marking a change in leadership at the top of one of the world's most valuable companies, and the fall of a key figure at the heart of the AI boom. Huang has been replaced by an interim CEO at Nvidia, previous chief financial officer Colette Kress. The company's share price has since shown signs of recovery since the announcement of his departure, after dropping considerably during the tumult caused by the initial allegations, and the uncertainty regarding Huang's future at the company. It's understood that the ex-Nvidia chief is scheduled to appear before the Senate Banking Committee alongside US commer…

title: 'I stand by Jensen': Nvidia employees come out in support of Huang after resignation
summary: The now ex-CEO co-founded the company over three decades ago.
body: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company after he admitted to an affair on Sunday , and allegations of a second affair came out on Wednesday . Now there are reports of a potential third . Though CTO Colette Kress has taken over in the interim, Nvidia seems to be shopping around for its next CEO, much to the dismay of some Nvidia staff, according to a report from Wired . It's claimed that a longtime engineer at Nvidia took to an internal suggestion box this week to ask the Nvidia board to consider the company's employees before deciding whether or not to get rid of Huang. This note was made prior to his resignation. However, over 1,600 comments have been left regarding this suggestion, the majority of which are apparently supportive of Huang. One says, "If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss." Another claims, "We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance." Notably, not all employees took to the suggestion box to air the same sentiment. One sent an email to the entire company saying, “I stand by Jensen. title: Paradox Interactive is getting a new boss as Fredrik Wester steps down for the second time
summary: Deputy CEO Mattias Lilja is taking the reins in January.
body: Paradox Interactive is getting a new boss: Deputy CEO Mattias Lilja will take over from current CEO Fredrik Wester in January 2027, a move Paradox said "is a natural evolution of how the company is already led." "My plan was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the company’s journey," Wester said in today's announcement . "Since I returned as CEO, we’ve streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level." As his statement implies, this is his second tenure as Paradox CEO: He held the position from 2009 to 2018, when he resigned and was replaced by Ebba Ljungerud. But Ljungerud's tenure was rocky, and she resigned in 2021 over "differing views on the company's strategy going forward," at which point Wester returned to the role. In many ways, Lilja has been calling the CEO shots for a few years now anyway, while Wester's focus has increasingly been on Paradox's "long-ter…

title: Now Jensen's gone, Intel’s trouble finding a steady CEO should serve as cautionary tale to Nvidia’s board
summary: Huang's permanent replacement will have some massive shoes to fill.
body: Has there ever been a tech CEO quite like Jensen Huang? The Nvidia chief has been an emblematic figure to PC gamers for years, before transcending into one of the primary architects of the AI revolution. Regardless of whether you love or hate the technology, (and the financial behemoth that Nvidia has become), you have to admit that Huang has presided over a meteoric rise to the top, the likes of which the tech world has rarely seen. Now Huang, the Nvidia cofounder, figurehead, and global AI industry pillar, has announced his resignation . The admission of an affair with someone some people suspect to be a Chinese spy, followed days later by reports of another affair with an Nvidia employee, proved to be his undoing as Nvidia chief. Nvidia's share price has dropped significantly in recent weeks. Investors, likely looking for some sort of stability after the past few weeks of AI and tech company financial woes, seem shaken. In many ways, the situation is unprecedented, and it's hard to draw parallels. But now Huang has gone, it puts Nvidia in the unenviable position of finding someone to replace him at the top of the stack. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO for…

title: Nvidia stocks jump back up after ex-CEO Jensen Huang's ousting
summary: Nvidia's share price has seemingly grown by around 10% since pre-market trading lows.
body: This week has been a mess for Nvidia, with its CEO, Jensen Huang, admitting to an affair on Sunday , only for a second affair allegation to come out yesterday . Today, Nvidia shares started as low as $151 in pre-market trading, but have since bounced back to between $163 and $166 in the opening hours of Nasdaq trading after the announcement of Jensen Huang's retirement as CEO . One might assume a downward trajectory with Huang's resignation, and CFO Colette Kress replacing him, as it could flag instability to shareholders, but the stock price now sits where it once sat on Wednesday, November 11 at 5 PM ET. The Nvidia stock price has been unruly this week, dipping by $15 between Friday night and Monday morning, then climbing to $181 by the end of Monday, then once again dropping to $167 on Tuesday. But, importantly, this morning saw the worst trade open for Nvidia stock since June 2025, just before the memory crisis started. The jump from $151 to around $165 represents a 10% increase for the company. Naturally, stocks are a fickle business, and, famously, the 'dead cat bounce' effect describes a moment in a stock decline where it briefly recovers. But Nvidia, even with a big loss i…

title: 'I'm a big Zach Cregger fan': Angela Sant'Albano gushes about the Resident Evil movie and likens Bryan to her own Grace Ashcroft
summary: Grace and Bryan—two peas in a very scared pod.
body: Resident Evil Requiem's director, Koshi Nakanishi, once said that putting Leon Kennedy in a horror game simply wouldn't work because "he wouldn't jump at something like a bucket falling. No one wants to see Leon scared by everything". And he was right, I couldn't have felt safer with Leon in Requiem. Grace on the other hand, we were decidedly less safe in her hands. But that didn't mean I enjoyed my time with her any less. While Leon's segments in Requiem were pure unbridled feel-good action, Grace found herself in one exhilaratingly stressful situation after another, not unlike another Resident Evil protagonist who rocked up this year. I'm of course talking about Bryan Hodukavich from Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie. (Image credit: Sony Pictures) One of my favourite parts of the Resident Evil film was just how ordinary Bryan was , it not only made it infinitely scarier (especially the first part) but I felt empathy for this poor delivery driver in a way that I probably wouldn't for a trained bioweapon killing machine. I hadn't actually thought about how alike Grace and Bryan are in this way, not until Grace's actress Angela Sant'Albano pointed it out herself during an intervie…

title: Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia's new interim CEO?
summary: With Jensen Huang gone, someone has to fill his boots. That's Kress, for the time being.
body: Jensen Huang has resigned , and in his place is a familiar face for anyone that's listened to one of Nvidia's financial calls: it's the company's long-standing CFO, Colette Kress. But you might be excused as a gamer for never hearing about her; an earnings call isn't everybody's cup of tea. Colette Kress has been chief financial officer at Nvidia since 2013 . That's 13 years sat alongside Jensen in calls with investors and financial institutions to discuss how the company is doing. Kress has been in the role for the record highs of recent years, and the not-so-record lows of others, like the price plummets of '25, '21, and '18. Prior to her role at Nvidia, Kress was SVP and CFO at Cisco for a couple of years and Corporate VP at Microsoft for nearly five. She also worked at Texas Instruments—all the big hitters, then. Generally, Kress has stayed out of any contentious issues with the company, only occassionally commenting on the big issues during earnings calls. Like when the RTX 30-series was out of stock everywhere thanks to cryptocurrency mining (the mining had an impact on the company's financials in a slightly contentious way, too). Or ceaseless comments on the increasing dema…

summary: Here are all the games The Council voted on.
body: The happiest time of year is just around the corner, folks. The PC Gaming Show: Most Wanted sponsored by Pot Noodle will be airing December 3rd, and we'll be counting down The Council's 20 most anticipated games. There's one major change this year, though. We've gone from counting down the top 25 games to the top 20. We've made this decision to ensure each game gets its time in the spotlight, meaning the show will be more enjoyable to watch. Also, The Council have recently unionised and refuse to count more until we agree to give them bathroom breaks, which we simply will not do. The Council remains, as ever, an inscrutable bunch of journalists, developers, celebrities, creators, streamers, gaming luminaries, and just generally people whose opinion on videogames carries some weight. How we selected the nominees Each year, we knock our heads together and puzzle over how to whittle down the thousands of upcoming games into a list of just 100. body: There is also one excellent external candidate who has been very successful outside of Nvidia and offers both technical expertise and solid business management experience. Employees loved working for him. Either one would be great. November 11, 2026 We thought it might be coming, and it's here: Jensen Huang is no longer CEO of Nvidia , as he has resigned following an admitted affair , and an additional alleged one . It wasn't unexpected, and both before and after the announcement there has been a lot of talk about how it would be a bad decision and could spell very bad news for Nvidia. And, well, there's certainly some truth in that given we saw company share prices drop after reports of Huang's alleged second affair came to light. After perusing X for a while today, the general sentiment seems to be that Huang was so incredibly central to Nvidia that the company couldn't possibly do well without him. title: WoW: Forever's new Riverglades zone feels more like The Burning Crusade+ than Classic+, and you know what, I'm absolutely okay with that
summary: Close enough. Welcome back, Nagrand.
body: So I've been utterly consumed by WoW: Forever, which is a relief, because it's my job to write about it—and I've been powering ahead to 40, where a deeply oldschool grind to get my first mount awaits me. Before that, though, I had an absolutely lovely time futzing around The Riverglades, one of WoW: Forever's properly bespoke zones. As in, this thing wasn't in vanilla. This was cooked up and released in November. Having quested through most of it in a blissful fugue state with some friends, we each came to the conclusion that it all feels very 2007, rather than 2006. The Riverglades, which you can head to at about level 38, is saturated with quests. Even more so than the revamped and revisited zones from vanilla World of Warcraft. And while it absolutely has the classic zone's sense of scale, and none of these quests have the retail aura of on-rails cutscenes about them, I wasn't actually tasting vanilla . title: After cracking down on 'cheat' mods in Helldivers 2 and taking another Steam review beating, Arrowhead plans hotfix that should allow harmless cosmetics
summary: The move to a better anti-cheat has not been wholly embraced by players.
body: Helldivers 2, in the running for the most review-bombed game in history, got another Steam beating a few weeks back when Arrowhead announced a change in anti-cheat services that would break or disallow existing mods. The goal with the switch from GameGuard to Easy Anti-Cheat, as the studio explained at the time , was to combat mods that "create unfair advantages or negatively impact others," but it also acknowledged that mods it has no problems with, like cosmetic add-ons, would also be affected. The news went over like a lead balloon, prompting over 10,000 fresh negative Steam reviews and a "mostly negative" recent rating. Skimming the last few weeks of ratings, negative reviewers are either miffed about their broken mods, new and old bugs, or the perception that Arrowhead is attacking modders instead of fixing bugs. There was no reality where a community notorious for intensely boycotting everything it finds annoying was going to embrace stricter modding oversight, but Arrowhead did address the outcry in its latest Helldivers 2 developer blog . title: Giana Sisters developer Black Forest Games buys itself out of Embracer: 'Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred'
summary: According to the press release, "THQ Nordic and Black Forest Games continue to collaborate on game development tasks."
body: Black Forest Games, German developer of early Kickstarter success Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams, as well as remakes of the first two Destroy All Humans games, and, er, Bubsy: The Woolies Strike Back, has announced it's leaving THQ Nordic after nine years within the Embracer Group subsidiary. Following a management buyout, Black Forest has founded an indie studio group called Third Signal. "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred," said Third Signal's founder and CEO Andreas Tobler. "Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer-driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life." Black Forest Games was founded by staff of Spellbound Entertainment, creator of the Desperados series and Arcania: Gothic 4 before being closed in 2012. title: Marvel Rivals' creative director addresses hate speech controversy and promises 'we've ramped up our disciplinary measures'
summary: A September incident that saw hate speech removed from the game's reporting system "sparked massive controversy in the community."
body: A few months ago Marvel Rivals became embroiled in one of the biggest controversies in its history when an error during an update ended up removing the "Hate Speech" option in its reporting system. This unfortunately led to a huge rise in slurs and hate speech within the game, and it also damaged the relationship between NetEase and players as many felt the studio wasn't doing enough to provide adequate safeguards for players . Little was said about the issue at the time, although it was corrected fairly quickly and NetEase promised harsher penalties for toxic behaviour a few weeks later. Now Marvel Rivals' creative director Guangyun Chen has explained what exactly went wrong and what the team is doing to rectify the issue in a recent dev diary : (Image credit: NetEase / Marvel) "In mid September, while optimising our report system UI, we made a configuration error that caused the 'Hate Speech' option to be replaced by 'Crime'. The moment we discovered the issue, we fixed it immediately—it was an oversight on our part." Mistakes happen, but what matters more is that NetEase is now trying to do more to combat hate speech in Marvel Rivals. "This incident sparked massive controversy …
